meta.subtitle: Margins and cash conversion have caught up with the story; at 36.8x trailing earnings the shares now need FY27E delivery

analystSentiment.commentary:
GE Aerospace reported Q2'26 revenue of $13.3B, {+ +21.1% YoY +}, at an operating margin of 18.6%. Operating margin has risen in each of FY23, FY24 and FY25, and the debate is now mostly about price.

At $312.04 the shares trade on 36.8x trailing earnings and 29.1x EV/EBITDA, and on ~31.8x consensus FY27E EPS of $9.82. Our BUY needs two things: FY27E delivery, and the market paying more for those earnings than it does today as FY27E becomes the near-term base.

We set a $330–$390 target range, below the street, for reasons we set out under Valuation; the risks follow in the summary below.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
General Electric Company, doing business as GE Aerospace, designs and produces commercial and defense aircraft engines, integrated engine components, electric power and aircraft systems. Its company description lists two segments: Commercial Engines & Services, which builds jet engines and provides maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) services and spare parts, and Defense & Propulsion Technologies, which serves governments, militaries and commercial airframers under brands including Avio Aero, Unison, Dowty Propellers and Colibrium Additive.

The company is based in Evendale, Ohio. FY25 revenue was $45.9B and FY25 net income was $8.7B. The market capitalization is ~$323.8B at a share price of $312.04.

thesis.label: BUY
thesis.body: GE Aerospace lifted its operating margin to 18.6% in FY25, and free cash flow rose from $3.7B in FY24 to $7.3B in FY25. **The thesis is that FY27E consensus is achievable and that the multiple on FY27E earnings rises toward the trailing level once they are the near-term base.** We rate the shares BUY with a $330–$390 target range. The counter-case is valuation: the stock already discounts sustained double-digit growth, so a re-rating needs the growth to arrive on schedule.

catalysts: The next quarterly report: revenue growth near the Q2'26 pace would run ahead of the consensus FY26E path.
Revisions to FY27E consensus EPS, the anchor of our Base case.
Any change in the repurchase pace, which drives per-share earnings growth.
risks: Valuation: a 36.8x trailing P/E leaves little room for a growth miss.
Liquidity: the trailing current ratio is below one.
Capital allocation: the buyback pace relative to free cash flow, discussed under Management.

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December.

financials.incomeCommentary:
Revenue grew from $35.3B in FY23 to $38.7B in FY24 and $45.9B in FY25, with growth of {+ +9.5% +} in FY24 and {+ +18.5% +} in FY25. Operating income rose faster, lifting the operating margin from 10.5% in FY23 to 13.8% in FY24 and 18.6% in FY25. That is operating leverage: profit grew faster than revenue in each year.

The latest quarter extends the run. Q2'26 revenue was $13.3B, {+ +21.1% YoY +}, and the quarter's operating margin matched the FY25 level. On a trailing-twelve-month basis the operating margin is 18.1% and the net margin is 17.7%.

Net income needs care. It exceeded operating income in each of FY23, FY24 and FY25, at $9.5B, $6.6B and $8.7B, so non-operating items lifted the bottom line in every year. The pack does not let us size those items, so we anchor recurring earnings to operating income rather than to net income or diluted EPS. Gross margin is not available in our data, so we cannot separate pricing from mix within the margin gains.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December.

financials.balanceCommentary:
Total debt has been stable at $22.0B in FY23, $21.3B in FY24 and $22.2B in FY25, after a step up from FY22. We do not have cash and short-term investments, so we cannot state net debt or a net leverage ratio, and we do not infer one.

Total equity fell from $28.6B in FY23 to $19.6B in FY24 and $18.9B in FY25. Share repurchases over the same two years were $5.8B and $7.6B. In FY24, net income more than covered that year's buyback, so repurchases explain only part of the FY24 equity decline. The pack does not show the remainder, and we do not assign a cause.

Liquidity is the weak point. The current ratio slid from 1.33 in FY23 to 1.09 in FY24 and 1.04 in FY25, and it stands at {- 0.98 -} on a trailing basis. A ratio below one means current liabilities exceed current assets. We have no breakdown of current liabilities, so we cannot say what drives it.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December.

financials.cashflowCommentary:
Operating cash flow rose from $4.7B in FY24 to $8.5B in FY25, while capital expenditure was $1.3B in FY25. Free cash flow reached $7.3B in FY25, against $4.3B in FY23 and $3.7B in FY24, and the FCF margin moved from 12.2% to 9.5% and then {+ 15.8% +}.

Share repurchases, set out beside equity above, are the main use of cash the pack shows. Dividends paid are not available in our data.

At the current price the trailing FCF yield is 2.6%. That is a thin cash return for a holder today, so the investment case depends on growth rather than on the current cash yield.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
On trailing numbers GE Aerospace trades at 36.8x earnings, 6.4x sales and 29.1x EV/EBITDA. We have no peer multiples on a comparable basis, so we judge the multiple against the company's own growth rather than against a peer set.

The two forward P/E figures differ because they use different earnings periods: 39.5x on next-twelve-months earnings and ~31.8x on FY27E. The NTM multiple sitting above the trailing one is consistent with consensus FY26E EPS of $7.91 being below FY25 diluted EPS of $8.14. That comparison sets a consensus mean against reported diluted EPS, which carries the non-operating items noted under Financials, so it may not be like for like. Our Bull and Base cases rest on FY27E EPS of $9.82, and our Bear case on FY26E-level earnings.

The street is constructive: 22 analysts split Buy 18, Hold 3, Sell 1, with a consensus target of $396.81, a median of $400.00 and a range of $347.00–$450.00.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: FY27E EPS comes in comfortably above the $9.82 consensus as revenue runs ahead of $55.8B, and the market keeps paying close to the 39.5x NTM multiple on those higher earnings. The price moves into the upper part of the street target range.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: FY26E revenue of ~$50.3B arrives at the +10% consensus rate and FY27E consensus EPS is met. As FY27E becomes the near-term earnings base, the multiple on it settles a little below today's 36.8x trailing P/E.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Growth falls below the consensus path, the FY27E recovery slips and earnings stay near the $7.91 FY26E consensus for longer. The market applies about the ~31.8x it now pays on FY27E to those lower earnings, and the price breaks the $268.91 52-week low.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
We weight the Base case at 50% and the Bull and Bear cases at 25% each. The Base price of $355 sits inside our target range.

The Bull case at $430 needs two things at once: FY27E earnings ahead of consensus and a multiple held near the NTM level. The Bear case at $255 needs the FY27E recovery to slip; neither step requires a collapse in the business.

Our range sits below the consensus and median street targets. The street's targets sit closer to our Bull price than to our Base, and we give the Bear outcome the same weight as the Bull, because thin liquidity and a premium multiple make the downside path as plausible as the upside one. The weighted outcome still clears the current price by enough for a BUY.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Our financial data reports GE Aerospace as a single reportable segment, with FY25 revenue of $45.9B. The company description instead lists two segments, Commercial Engines & Services and Defense & Propulsion Technologies. The two sources disagree, and we use the single consolidated figure; we quote no segment or regional split.

moatFactors.name: Aftermarket services
moatFactors.body: The company description pairs new engine sales with MRO services and spare parts, which ties revenue to the fleet already in service rather than to new deliveries alone. The pack does not let us attribute the FY23 to FY25 operating margin gains to services, so we rate the factor Moderate; a service revenue or margin split showing services carrying the margin would support a Strong rating.

moatFactors.name: Defense and component breadth
moatFactors.body: Serving governments and militaries alongside commercial airframers gives the company demand that does not rest on airline traffic alone. The counter-case: with no segment revenue, we cannot size the defense share, so we cannot size that diversification either.

moatFactors.name: Cash generation
moatFactors.body: The FCF margin was 15.8% in FY25, after 12.2% in FY23 and 9.5% in FY24. FY25 free cash flow covered capital expenditure but not the full repurchase program. One strong year after a weaker one does not establish that cash conversion is durable, which is why we rate this factor Moderate.

businessMoat.durability:
We rate the moat NARROW. The evidence available to us, margin expansion and free cash flow, supports a competitive advantage, but it covers a short run of years and comes without the installed-base, backlog or segment data that would show how long the advantage lasts. A WIDE rating would need that evidence.

The main threat to durability is not a named competitor but the cycle in commercial aviation and in government defense budgets. Neither is guaranteed.

points: Second-quarter pace: Q2'26 revenue of $13.3B grew {+ +21.1% YoY +}, ahead of FY25's {+ +18.5% +}. That is one quarter set against a full-year rate, not yet a trend.

Counter-case: consensus FY26E revenue of ~$50.3B implies +10% growth, well below the Q2'26 pace. The street expects a clear slowdown, and our Base case accepts that path rather than betting against it.
FY27E is the earnings step: consensus has revenue of $55.8B and EPS of $9.82 for FY27E, a step up from the FY26E consensus discussed under Valuation. That step underpins our Base case.

Fleet in service, unconfirmed: the aftermarket tie noted under the moat could lift revenue as the fleet grows. We have no installed-base data, so this is a hypothesis we do not build into our numbers.
Per-share growth from repurchases: buybacks shrink the share count, so EPS can grow faster than net income as long as the program continues.

management.leadership: The proxy statement excerpt available to us, dated 2026-03-12, covers related-person transactions and does not name the company's directors or officers, so we do not name or assess individuals. The record shows operating margin rising in FY24 and FY25, and free cash flow conversion improving in FY25 after weakening in FY24. Without a proxy excerpt naming officers, or MD&A, we do not attribute those results to individuals.
management.capitalAllocation:
Capital allocation has leaned heavily on repurchases. FY25 repurchases of $7.6B exceeded free cash flow of $7.3B, and FY24 repurchases of $5.8B exceeded that year's $3.7B, while total debt stayed broadly flat at $22.2B in FY25. The 0.60% dividend yield makes the dividend a small use of cash beside the buyback.

We would prefer repurchases matched to free cash flow at a 36.8x trailing P/E; buying back stock at a premium multiple returns less per dollar than at a lower one. The counterpoint is that FY25 free cash flow came close to covering the program, so the FY25 gap is small. Without a cash balance in the pack, we cannot say what funded the shortfall.
management.governance:
Under the 2026-03-12 proxy statement, the Governance Committee reviews and approves related-person transactions above $120,000. The proxy reports none since January 1, 2025, except that Fidelity, a five percent or greater shareholder, or its affiliates served as recordkeeper or directed trustee for certain company retirement plans and received approximately $5.1 million for these services in 2025.

For a holder, this means a large shareholder also earns fees from the company. The fee is small beside the company's scale and the arrangement was disclosed, but it is a commercial tie a holder may weigh alongside Fidelity's voting position. The excerpt is truncated and does not cover board composition, director independence or executive pay, so we make no claim about any of them.
management.insiderOwnership: The proxy statement excerpt available to us does not include director or officer ownership, so we make no claim about insider alignment.

idiosyncratic: Valuation compression: at 36.8x trailing earnings and 29.1x EV/EBITDA, a slowdown in growth or a margin stall could cut the multiple faster than earnings can grow into it. This is the core of our Bear case.
Estimate risk: our Base case rests on consensus FY27E EPS of $9.82. A cut to that estimate would remove the earnings step the current multiple leans on.
Liquidity and leverage: with total debt of $22.2B, a trailing current ratio below one and no cash figure available to us, we cannot confirm the cushion against a downturn.
Buyback funding: the repurchase pace set out under capital allocation would need debt or a cut to the program in a weaker cash year.
risks.systemic: The cyclical exposures named under the moat, air travel for the aftermarket and government budgets for defense, are the main macro risks here. A richly valued industrial is also sensitive to interest rates and to the market's appetite for long-duration growth: a rise in discount rates can compress the multiple even if the company delivers on its estimates.

body: We rate GE Aerospace BUY with a $330–$390 target range. Operating margin and FY25 cash conversion have improved, and FY27E consensus gives the current price a path to support.
The rating is a measured one: our Base price of $355 sits above the $312.04 share price, but the reward/risk across our scenarios is 0.64×, so the downside is not small beside the upside.

What would change our view: revenue growth running below the +10% consensus FY26E rate, FY27E consensus EPS falling away from $9.82, or a step-up in repurchases funded by a rise in total debt from the FY25 level would move us to HOLD.
